# Privacy

Transcript has no backend. There is no account, no analytics SDK, no advertising SDK, and no server belonging to us that your data passes through. You bring your own AI — an API key for a service you chose, a model on your own computer, or a model that runs on the phone itself — and the app talks to it directly from your device.

## What the app does with each kind of data

### Audio recordings

- **Where it goes:** Can be sent to the AI service the user chose
- **Kept on the device:** yes
- **Your controls:** Choose the transcription provider in Settings; delete a recording at any time from the library.

Recordings are saved on this device. If you pick a cloud service for speech-to-text, the audio is uploaded to that service — directly from this device, using your own account — so it can be transcribed. Pick on-device recognition or a downloaded Whisper model and the audio never leaves the phone.

### Transcripts

- **Where it goes:** Can be sent to the AI service the user chose
- **Kept on the device:** yes
- **Your controls:** Choose the notes provider in Settings.

The text of what was said is stored on this device. If you pick a cloud service to turn it into notes, the text is sent to that service. A model running on your own computer keeps it on your network instead.

### Notes, tasks and boards

- **Where it goes:** Stays on this device
- **Kept on the device:** yes
- **Your controls:** Export or delete anything, at any time.

Everything the app produces — summaries, action items, the board and the timeline — is stored on this device only. Exports go wherever you send them, which is up to you.

### API keys

- **Where it goes:** Stays on this device
- **Kept on the device:** yes
- **Your controls:** Remove a saved key in Settings.

Keys are held in the system keychain (iOS) or the encrypted Keystore (Android). They are sent only to the service they belong to, as part of a request you triggered. They are never written to logs, diagnostics or exports.

### Crash diagnostics

- **Where it goes:** Stays on this device
- **Kept on the device:** yes
- **Your controls:** View, share or delete crash reports in Settings.

If the app crashes, it writes a report to a file on this device. The report holds the error, the stack trace and recent app events, with keys and personal paths stripped out. It contains no recording or transcript text, and it is not uploaded — you decide whether to send it.

### Accounts and identifiers

- **Where it goes:** Stays on this device
- **Kept on the device:** no

There is no account to create and no sign-in. The app assigns no user or advertising identifier and contains no analytics or advertising SDK.

## Store listing answers

Copy these verbatim. They are generated from the same source the app itself reads, so they describe what the build actually does.

### App Store Connect — App Privacy

> No data collected. The app has no backend, no account system, no analytics and no advertising SDK. Recordings and transcripts are sent only to the AI provider the user selects, using the user's own API key, directly from the device — a user-directed transfer to a service the user has their own relationship with, not collection by this app or on its behalf.

### Google Play Console — Data safety

> No data collected and no data shared with the developer. Audio and transcripts may be transmitted to a third-party AI service, but only the one the user configures with their own credentials, and only to perform the transcription or summarisation the user requested. All app-generated content stays in app-private storage. Data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS); plain HTTP is permitted only for servers on the user's own local network.
